sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort five-date panel with treatment adoption at date \(3\), a finite active state space of size \(m\), a common absorbing exit, known \(J\leq m\), and possible date-\(1\) absorption in the headline class.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete five-date panels on the \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^{5}m^r\)-cell absorption-legal support; \(N_2=126\).
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\), and units absorbed by date \(1\) have identical absorbed potential continuations.
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability. Positive active masses \(\alpha_j^d\) and hence positive full masses \(\pi_j^d\) are derived from anchor-star nonsingularity, not separately assumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted. Empirical frequencies on the fixed \(N_m\)-cell support feed the guarded analytic anchor-star recovery map.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 14 reconstructs latent transition components under its stated full-rank and positive-transition conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Four anchor slices determine the spectral basis, and the observable anchor-star slices transport recovery to all active states at the excluded common-absorbing boundary.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 reconstructs Markov-mixture components under its time-homogeneous and component-rank conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The known-J theorem uses selected active minors and stochastic normalization without time homogeneity and does not claim to subsume that reconstruction theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies homogeneous Markov-mixture reconstruction under its state-count and nondegeneracy restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present result is causal, time-varying, permits an absorbing boundary, and treats fixed known J no larger than the active-state count.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper develops aggregate duration difference-in-differences under absorption-oriented restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present theorem reconstructs latent-type multi-state contributions and isolates the initial-absorber frontier for conditional effects.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization and derives regular asymptotics for estimated weights.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The analytic-gradient theorem differentiates the known-J anchor-star row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map on the absorption-legal support.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration permit arbitrary correlation when marginal variances are positive.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The uniform-band theorem adds the buffered empirical guard and quantile continuity at singular correlation limits for this fixed-dimensional recovery map.

body.tldr: For a finite active state space of size \(m\) and a known type count \(2\leq J\leq m\), four anchor slices determine the spectral basis and \(2m-1\) observable anchor-star selected minors transport it to every active state. Projectors, stochastic row sums, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse, and a full-predecessor-row transport formula recover active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate first-post ATT despite a common absorbing state and possible initial absorption. Anchor-star nonsingularity itself implies positive active and full type masses. The no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface additionally identifies full type shares and conditional type effects. The resulting \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^5m^r\)-cell map has an explicit saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands under singular correlation; no restricted-model efficiency claim is made.

project_justification.gap: Published short-panel Markov-mixture reconstruction and the adjacent transition-independence theorem use rank, positivity, homogeneity, or state-count conditions that do not cover the common-absorbing boundary treated here. They also do not characterize the initial-absorber frontier: latent full shares and conditional type effects may fail while every type contribution and the aggregate remain identified.
project_justification.niche: With known \(J\leq m\), fixed ex ante \(J\)-row and \(J\)-column selections, and an observable anchor-star of nonsingular selected minors, four anchor slices identify the common spectral basis while the remaining star slices transport it across active states. Stochastic normalization handles exit, and absorption makes omitted initial absorbers a zero-effect component.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the explicit known-\(J\) projector, row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map; proves the active-versus-full identification frontier and a generic allocation counterexample; retains an exact rational \(J=m=2\) witness; and derives the analytic saturated gradient plus guarded uniform multiplier bands.

body.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, supply the closest causal inverse-cancellation architecture, but their stated full-rank and positive-transition class excludes the common absorbing boundary; this is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of their theorem. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their own homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; their scaling and label ideas are prior art, whereas this theorem is causal, time-varying, and uses known \(J\leq m\) selected anchor-star minors. Restricted hidden-Markov reconstruction results impose their own emission or structural restrictions and do not prove the potential-path contribution identity here. Deaner and Ku (2026) study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) are neighboring Gaussian bootstrap and anti-concentration references. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer only: this paper does not claim their data satisfy the latent Markov, rank, support, or iid assumptions. The deleted constrained-efficiency branch is not claimed in prose.
body.interpretation:
The generalized result distinguishes the full type share \(\pi_j^d\), the active share \(\alpha_j^d\), the unnormalized contribution \(
u_j\), and the at-risk effect \(\eta_j\). Anchor-star slices identify \(\alpha_j^d\), \(
u_j\), and \(\eta_j=
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), with positivity derived from nonsingularity. They cannot allocate already-absorbed zero-effect mass across latent labels, so full shares and full conditional effects need not be identified. If date-\(1\) absorption is absent, \(\pi_j^d=\alpha_j^d\) and \(	au_j=\eta_j\). Four anchor slices identify the spectral basis; recovery of every active row for \(J<m\) uses the full observable anchor star. Rao and Risch's incumbent-firm setting motivates the decomposition but is not reanalyzed here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the canonical-gradient bound only for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated finite-multinomial support-stratum model. The paper does not parameterize the smaller restricted Markov observed-law image, compute its score Jacobian, or claim its efficiency bound or an attaining estimator. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed Monte Carlo draw count needs separate approximation analysis. Weak eigengaps, changing selected-minor rank, unknown \(J\), clustered sampling, and approximate common kernels remain outside the result.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves a sufficient constructive frontier for fixed finite \(m\), known \(2\leq J\leq m\), fixed ex ante selected sets and anchor pairs, observable anchor-star nonsingularity, distinct common cycle signatures, cohort overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, absorption, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. It derives rather than assumes type positivity. It does not establish necessity beyond the explicit initial-absorber allocation family, identify unknown type count, handle weak or complex off-model spectra, justify dependent-panel inference, or exploit date \(4\) restrictions for efficiency. Full conditional type effects require no date-\(1\) absorption; the broad class identifies active sublaws, contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate.
